angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 5,833,445 km at 57.31 pc = 1.36 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 13288: distance 57.307 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.011), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 57.307 +/- 0.63 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 16.7930 +/- 0.2167 mas (same row, RUWE 1.44), 77.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 8.385 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 13288: radius 8.385 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 40.696 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.051) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 5,833,445 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5038 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 13288: effective temperature 5038 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.047) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 13288: effective temperature 5038 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.047) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * tau02 Eri: spectral type K0III (1988MSS...C04....0H)
luminositySource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5127513656557144576, flags_flame 10: lum_flame 44.448368 solar luminosities (16th to 84th percentiles 43.466854 to 45.52753); its log10 is recorded
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * tau02 Eri: projected rotation speed 1.11 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2015A&A...574A..50J)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.89 from 2024A&A...682A.145S; the 11 published values span log g 2.82 to 3.33, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...682A.145S)
